# Freeze store integrity maintenance

Ensure the `TextFileBasedViolationStore` maintains the integrity of its `stored.rules` index and files.

Setting `default.integrity` to `repair` will check the index and folder as they are on disk during initialization, even if the same folder was initialized before. Defaulting to `ignore` which checks nothing.

If an entry points to a path that is not a regular file directly within the folder, it is broken. This also applies if the file name is not a valid path.

If an entry is not broken and its file has no violations it is resolved. Files that only contain line breaks are also resolved.

Entries that point to the same file name are shared, even if nothing exists with that name. If multiple entries point to the same file they are also shared. Including through a symbolic or hard link. Even if that file is outside the folder.

The `TextFileBasedViolationStore` will not touch any shared entries or files that no entry points to. If an entry is shared and anything else it will remain shared.

When set to `repair` broken entries will be discarded.

When set to `repair` resolved entries and the file they point to will be discarded. If a resolved entry is a symbolic link the file it points to will be deleted as well.

If using `repair` and saving no violations for a known rule it will forget the rule. Its entry will be removed and its file as well. Unless another entry is sharing that file. In which case only the entry will be removed. Even if it points outside the folder. If using `repair` and saving no violations for an unknown rule nothing will be saved.

If it cannot delete the file of a rule it is forgetting it will fail to save and leave the entry.

   - Added support for the configuration property `default.integrity` (accessed via `integrity` in store properties), defaulting to `ignore` (no check).
   - When set to `repair`, the index and directory contents are inspected directly on disk upon store initialization, even if the folder was initialized before.

2. **Classification & Repair on Initialization**:
   - **Broken entries**: An entry is classified as broken if its path is not a valid path or does not point to a regular file directly inside the store folder (e.g. non-existent file, directory, or path traversing outside). When in `repair` mode, broken entries are discarded from `stored.rules` without deleting any filesystem targets.
   - **Resolved entries**: An entry is classified as resolved if it is not broken and its referenced file contains no violations (empty or containing only line breaks). In `repair` mode, resolved entries are removed from `stored.rules` and their files are deleted. If a resolved entry points to a symbolic link, both the symbolic link and its target file are deleted.
   - **Shared entries**: Entries are classified as shared if they reference the same file name (even if non-existent) or point to the same file (e.g. via hard link or symbolic link, including targets outside the store folder). Shared entries and unreferenced files (files in the folder not referenced by any entry) are never deleted or modified during initialization; if an entry is shared and also broken/resolved, it remains shared.

3. **Saving with Repair**:
   - In `repair` mode, when saving zero violations for an unknown rule, nothing is saved.
   - When saving zero violations for a known rule, the rule is forgotten:
     - If the file is shared with another entry, only the rule's index entry is removed from `stored.rules`.
     - If the file is not shared, the file (and its symlink target if applicable) is deleted, and the entry is removed from `stored.rules`.
     - If deleting the file fails (e.g., due to filesystem permissions), a [`StoreUpdateFailedException`](file:///app/archunit/src/main/java/com/tngtech/archunit/library/freeze/StoreUpdateFailedException.java) is thrown and the entry is left untouched in `stored.rules`.

4. **Tests Added**:
   - Added unit tests in [`TextFileBasedViolationStoreTest`](file:///app/archunit/src/test/java/com/tngtech/archunit/library/freeze/TextFileBasedViolationStoreTest.java) covering:
     - Default `ignore` behavior.
     - Discarding broken entries on `repair`.
     - Discarding resolved entries and deleting files (including symlink targets) on `repair`.
     - Preserving shared entries (same filename, hard links, symlinks outside folder) and unreferenced files.
     - Repairing on disk even if previously initialized.
     - Saving 0 violations for unknown rules (nothing saved).
     - Saving 0 violations for known rules (forgetting rule and deleting file).
     - Saving 0 violations for shared files (only removing entry).
     - Deletion failure leaving entry intact.
   - Added integration test in [`FreezingArchRuleTest`](file:///app/archunit/src/test/java/com/tngtech/archunit/library/freeze/FreezingArchRuleTest.java#L519-L537) verifying rules are forgotten upon zero violations when `integrity` is `repair`.
